says: Scenario: A node goes quiet
The project is brought back to its declared state.
Host A runs the swarm: the master, which keeps the names, and node-1, which renews its lease with the master every few seconds.
node-1 is frozen: its container paused. It says nothing, and no graceful path sees it.
The master hears nothing from node-1. When its lease runs out, node-1 is flagged absent: a dashed ring. Its name and records stay, flagged.
A request to node-1 now is refused at once, not left waiting on its address.
Refused: absent: /hosts/node-1/node, since 2026-11-02T18:24:21.637Z
node-1 is thawed. Its next heartbeat reaches the master, and it is present again.
A request to node-1 is answered again.
node-1 is stopped gracefully: it leaves the master's names first, so its name is free at once.
The swarm runs on: a request to the master's own repository is answered.
Scenario finished.

Scenario: A node on another host
The project is brought back to its declared state.
Host A runs the swarm: the master and node-1, both controlled by host A's manager.
Host A gives host B an invitation: public facts only, no secret.
Host B's own manager starts its node from the invitation, provisions it from host B's vault, on host B's own management network.
remote-1 is part of the swarm, reached by name, but host A does not control it: it is outlined on the map.
A request from host A crosses to remote-1's repository: in as a bundle, out on its main.
remote-1 writes a note in its own repository: activity its replicas see.
Host B's manager stops remote-1, gracefully.
The swarm runs on: a request from host A to node-1 is still answered.
Scenario finished.
